workPackageTitle: Exact PCG32 implementation, SplitMix64 child derivation, registered stream families, recovery state, scripted test sources
notes: Entries are added before implementation and are never renumbered (docs/technical/91 § Verification registry). This file is the first commit of the W1-SIM stream: no SIM production type or test class named by a selector below exists yet.
The structural validator for this file is owned by TASK-FND-009-002. Until it lands, the shape here matches tests/verification/FND-002.json and tests/verification/FND-003.json exactly.

Status is current status: every entry is 'registered' because no implementing task has landed. A later commit flips an entry to 'implemented' only when its selector actually runs and passes, as tests/verification/FND-002.json and tests/verification/FND-003.json do.

Every nunit selector is a fully qualified 'Namespace.Class.Method' so one entry names exactly one test method. Test namespaces mirror production namespaces per doc 114 § Naming and file-placement defaults; the full type and method layout the implementation must produce is fixed in the W1-SIM design contract handed to the implementation tasks.

doc 110 registers the SIM work packages but not their task IDs. SIM-005 splits into TASK-SIM-005-001, the algorithm and derivation (PCG32 generator, the SplitMix64-style Mix function and the d0/d1/state-seed/selector chain, the registered family key table, the stream set derived from a master seed and schema version), and TASK-SIM-005-002, the consumption and lifecycle layer (bounded conversion, canonical selection, injectable source, recovery state). The split is the one doc 110's completion gate already implies by listing golden vectors separately from bounded conversion, stable sequences, serialization, and independence.

No test in this package uses the shared DeterministicCase harness. Every assertion here is deterministic by construction - a pinned seed, a pinned family and instance key, and a committed golden - so there is no randomized body to log a harness seed for. DeterministicCase supplies test-harness randomness (System.Random) and is unrelated to the authoritative stream contract this package implements.

VER-SIM-005-004 is the entry that keeps the goldens honest. A golden vector regenerated from the same implementation it is meant to constrain proves only self-consistency; doc 91 § Reference models requires deliberately simple independent logic where one implementation could repeat its own bug. The committed vectors must be reproduced by a second implementation written directly from doc 20 § Authoritative random-number contract, and the gate fails if either implementation changes alone.

doc 20 § Authoritative random-number contract registers 23 family keys. VER-SIM-005-010 asserts all 23 with their exact hex values; a new authoritative draw is a new registered key in doc 20 and a new entry here, never a reused key.

The golden fixtures named below are the vector files under tests/MechaMiner.Simulation.Tests/Goldens/, each of which declares its authority, the random schema version it pins, and the fact that it was derived by a reference implementation independent of the C# code under test. Two decisions doc 20 leaves open are fixed in those file headers rather than in code comments: the rejection-sampling threshold for bounded integers and the bit layout of the 53-bit [0,1) conversion. VER-SIM-005-005 and VER-SIM-005-006 assert exactly those decisions, so changing either is a golden change under doc 91 § Determinism and fixture policy and not a local implementation choice.

One guard in the random path is structurally unreachable from any public entry point, so nothing in this file verifies it, and its reason is stated as something someone could try to falsify, naming the grep that would do it, because a label is the one claim in this file no negative control can test. Pcg32.Restore's even-increment refusal. Pcg32 is internal and there is no InternalsVisibleTo in this repository, which Random/RandomSchemaVersion.cs:26 states and which is the only occurrence of the string, so no assembly outside MechaMiner.Simulation holds one. Inside it, Restore's only caller is RandomStreamSet.Restore, which takes its increment from a RandomStreamRecoveryState whose public constructor already refuses an even increment, the refusal VER-SIM-005-014 exercises. To falsify: add a second caller of Pcg32.Restore that does not obtain its increment from a RandomStreamRecoveryState, or construct such a state with an even increment. Grep: 'Pcg32', '.Restore('. The record type is therefore where an even increment is actually refused, and Pcg32.Restore's copy of the same check cannot fire. It is kept rather than deleted, and Pcg32 is not exported in order to test it, because the odd-increment invariant belongs to the generator that depends on it as much as to the record that carries it.

The 'platforms' list records the platforms an entry has actually been executed on, not the platforms its subject is intended to support, following tests/verification/FND-001.json and FND-002.json, which state the same convention and were corrected to it. On that reading windows-x64 and osx-arm64 are declared applicable and unexercised for every entry in this file: the subjects are portable .NET with no platform-conditional code, so they are expected to hold there, and that expectation is not coverage. linux-x64 is the only platform any run has covered. The linux-x64 result is now a runner's record and not only a local invocation: workflow 'fast suite' run 31097680603, job 'fast (bootstrap, format-check, build, test-fast, godot-import)', completed successfully on head 5a3f3ac at 2026-08-06T11:38:04Z on a pinned ubuntu-24.04 runner, reporting test-fast total 147, passed 147, failed 0, skipped 0. Read that as covering the merged tree rather than this branch's tree: .github/workflows/fast.yml is not in this branch at all, it is on the base branch, and a pull_request event resolves workflows from the merge of head into base, so what ran green is the tree that would land. This branch's own commit has never been run alone by a runner, and a push to it starts no workflow, because its tree contains none. The retained artifact under artifacts/verbs/ still names the local invocation and its source_revision. Adding a platform back to any entry here requires a real run on it, which needs a runner FND-005 owns. No entry field holds 'applicable but unexercised': doc 91 § Verification registry lists the accepted fields and there is no 'pendingPlatforms', so this note is where the applicability claim lives rather than a field invented for it.

tests/verification/SIM-negative-controls.md, a sibling of this file, is the whole negative-control record for the seven SIM packages: for each control the perturbation, the exact command, the exact failure text, and the forced-rebuild method that makes a transcript a claim about a build rather than about a source file. It is committed rather than cited from a reviewer's scratch directory, because a path only one person can open is not evidence; the transcripts that used to live in five session evidence files outside the repository are now in it. It is not scoped by an evidenceKinds value: the entries whose control it records name it in their own fixtures, qualified by section. Its "Which entry each section controls" table is the index over all seven files and is authoritative for what follows. In this file 9 entries name it: VER-SIM-005-001, VER-SIM-005-002, VER-SIM-005-004, VER-SIM-005-005, VER-SIM-005-009, VER-SIM-005-010, VER-SIM-005-011, VER-SIM-005-013, VER-SIM-005-016. The two pointers this file previously recorded as owed, VER-SIM-005-011 and VER-SIM-005-013, are now made. 7 entries name it nowhere because no transcript records a control for them: VER-SIM-005-003, VER-SIM-005-006, VER-SIM-005-007, VER-SIM-005-008, VER-SIM-005-012, VER-SIM-005-014, VER-SIM-005-015. That is the largest uncovered set of the seven files, and it is a real limit rather than an accounting artifact: this package's gates lean on committed goldens and an independent reference implementation, so their evidence is agreement with an external oracle rather than a demonstration that a gate can fail. VER-SIM-005-016 names two sections. The first, § SIM-005's permanent negative control, with its reference stub repaired, is the transcript of this entry's own test failing: the repair-the-stub control the other six packages' permanent negative-control entries have was run for this one too, with the reference stream no longer dropping the increment's mandatory low bit, so the mutation the test injects is no longer caught and the assertion has nothing left to report. Seven of seven rather than six. The second, § Randomness: the algorithm constants, it keeps as the cross-reference the document labels it: that section applies to production the same one-bit changes this entry applies to the test-side reference, and it does not show this entry's own test failing.

On 'negative-control' in evidenceKinds. doc 91 § What a kind may name rules that a technique is not a kind, and excludes the value from the minted inventory a kind must be added to before it may appear in a registry file, so it is a defect to correct in this file rather than a value grandfathered into it. Correcting it is a removal and not a substitution, because a negative control's evidence is not a different form of thing from an ordinary test's: a control run as an NUnit test produces exactly the artifact form a positive NUnit test produces. So an affected entry takes the kind its artifact form already gives it, which is the kind it already carries: 'test-counts' with 'test-output' for an nunit selector, the pair 53 positive nunit entries of that shape across these registries carry, and 'golden-text' with 'test-counts' and 'text-diff' for a golden comparison, the shape 11 positive entries carry. Nothing is minted, no kind is added, and no entry loses a kind its evidence needs. What the label carried is that the gate has a negative control, which is a fact about the gate and not about the form of its evidence, so it is required here to appear in prose that can say what a label could not: the entry summary names the perturbation injected and what was observed, and where tests/verification/SIM-negative-controls.md records that control the entry's fixtures name it, qualified by section, so the entry's own pointer reaches the transcript rather than only the artifact that cannot demonstrate a control. Summary text in these files is otherwise not reworded; the integration owner authorized 'summary or notes' for this correction specifically, and summary is the only per-entry prose field available, because doc 91 § Verification registry lists the accepted entry fields and no per-entry 'notes' is among them, while doc 115 § Schema registry has SCH-QUA-001 reject unknown fields. A field invented to hold it would repeat exactly the coining that produced this defect.

entries.summary: PCG32 output matches the committed golden vector exactly: state advances modulo 2^64 with multiplier 6364136223846793005, and each output is the XSH-RR transformation of the prior state - xorshift by 18 then 27, rotated by the prior state's top five bits - for a pinned state and odd increment.

The seed-derivation chain matches the committed golden vector exactly: Mix, then d0 from the master seed and schema version, d1 from d0 and the family key, the state seed from d1 and the instance key, and the selector from the state seed, with every step wrapping modulo 2^64.
fixtures: tests/verification/SIM-negative-controls.md § The Mix shift, against a published external value

entries.summary: Stream initialization matches the committed golden vector exactly: state zero and increment (selector shifted left one bit) OR 1, advance once, add the state seed modulo 2^64, advance once more, and only then return the first caller-visible value.

The committed golden vectors were confirmed against an independent derivation rather than self-consistency: a second, deliberately simple implementation written from doc 20 alone reproduces every vector, and the gate fails if either implementation is changed without the other.
fixtures: tests/verification/SIM-negative-controls.md § Randomness: rejection sampling replaced by modulo reduction

entries.summary: Bounded integers are unbiased by rejection sampling, not modulo reduction: for a bound that does not divide 2^32, every raw draw above the largest exact multiple of the bound is rejected and redrawn, the residue distribution over an enumerated window is exactly uniform, and the consumed-draw count exceeds the sample count.
fixtures: tests/verification/SIM-negative-controls.md § Randomness: rejection sampling replaced by modulo reduction

entries.summary: Exactly one 53-bit conversion to a double in [0,1) exists, it matches its committed golden, and it returns neither 1.0 nor a negative value for any input draw including all-zero and all-ones bit patterns.

A chance representable as an integer ratio compares integers and consumes exactly one draw: it does not route through the double conversion, and its boundary cases at ratio zero and ratio one consume no draw at all.

Selection from an empty or singleton collection consumes no draw: the stream's state, increment, and consumed-draw count are identical before and after, so adding a guaranteed-outcome selection cannot shift any later sequence.

Canonical selection establishes candidate order before drawing an index: two collections holding the same members in different insertion order select the same member from the same stream state, so no selection depends on dictionary or scene enumeration.

All 23 registered stream families of doc 20 are present with their exact hex family keys, every key is unique, the documented instance-key rule is declared for each, and deriving a stream for an unregistered family key is rejected rather than silently succeeding.

Stream families are independent: two families derived from the same master seed share no state, drawing from one does not advance the other, and inserting an extra draw into one family leaves every other family's sequence bit-identical.

tests/verification/SIM-negative-controls.md § The family key is dropped from the derivation

entries.summary: Instance keys separate instances within one family: two instance keys yield independent sequences, the same instance key reproduces the same sequence, and a family whose registered instance key is zero rejects a nonzero instance key rather than deriving an unregistered stream.

Recovery round-trips every instantiated authoritative stream: state and odd increment serialize and restore exactly, and a restored stream produces the identical continuation of the sequence the original would have produced.
fixtures: tests/verification/SIM-negative-controls.md § Controls for the second review pass
tests/verification/SIM-negative-controls.md § Recovery re-derives the stream instead of carrying its live state

entries.summary: A recovery artifact carrying a different random schema version is rejected as incompatible rather than resumed, and the presentation-only family is never written into the recovery state at all.

A test may inject a scripted source but production cannot select an alternate algorithm: the production stream set exposes no algorithm or source parameter, and a scripted source that runs out of scripted values fails loudly rather than falling back to a real generator.

A negative control proves the golden and independence gates can fail: a one-bit change to the multiplier, to either xorshift amount, to the rotation, and to the increment's low bit each make VER-SIM-005-001 through VER-SIM-005-003 fail, and a shared-state stub makes VER-SIM-005-011 fail.
